The `mailkit` package crashes when building an email on a machine whose hostname contains non-ASCII characters while the message uses a non-unicode encoding. Reproduce: with `mailkit.utils.CachedDnsName` (i.e. `DNS_NAME`) resolving to a non-ASCII hostname such as `'漢字'`, constructing an `EmailMessage` and calling `.message()` with `email.encoding = 'iso-8859-1'` raises a UnicodeEncodeError because the Message-ID header embeds the raw non-ASCII domain. The domain must be converted to its ASCII-compatible Punycode form (IDN -> ACE) before it is used in the header, so the Message-ID should contain the punycode label (e.g. `xn--p8s937b` for `漢字`).

Notice that the IDN-to-ASCII conversion idiom `domain.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` is already copy-pasted inline in several places across the package (the URL validator, the email address sanitizer, and the urlize helper), and the real bug is that the hostname lookup in `mailkit/utils.py` never applies that conversion at all.

Fix this the right way by REMOVING the duplication: add a single shared helper `punycode(domain)` to `mailkit/encoding.py` that returns `domain.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`, and then update EVERY place that needs IDN->ASCII conversion to import and call that one helper instead of inlining the idiom. Concretely: (1) `mailkit/encoding.py` gains `def punycode(domain)`; (2) `mailkit/validators.py`, `mailkit/message.py`, and `mailkit/html.py` each replace their inline `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` with a call to `punycode(...)`; and (3) `mailkit/utils.py`'s `CachedDnsName.get_fqdn` is changed to run the looked-up hostname through `punycode(...)` so the non-ASCII hostname bug is actually fixed. After the change, the inline idiom must live in only one place (the helper). Do NOT change `mailkit/http.py` or `mailkit/version.py`; the IDNA-looking line in `mailkit/http.py` is unrelated legacy/dead code that must stay exactly as is. All existing behavior (valid URLs, ASCII domains, urlize output) must keep working.
